name: The ten spies
charge: Bringing an evil report; making the congregation to murmur
summary: Twelve men searched Canaan forty days. Ten came back and told the people the land eats its inhabitants and the giants made them as grasshoppers. Caleb and Joshua said the Lord would bring them in. The people believed the ten.
offense: They were sent as rulers of their tribes, and they searched the land forty days (Numbers 13:2, 25), and their report did not deny the land was good, for they carried back one cluster of grapes borne between two upon a staff and said, surely it floweth with milk and honey (Numbers 13:23, 27). What they denied was that God could give it, and they said it in the presence of the whole congregation: we be not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we (Numbers 13:31). Then they brought up an evil report of the land, calling it a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof, and there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight (Numbers 13:32-33). Ten rulers who had watched Egypt destroyed and the sea part measured themselves against men, and the evil report spread its spirit through the whole camp in a night. Caleb had already answered them in front of the people: let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it (Numbers 13:30).
judgment: Because of the report the whole congregation wept that night, said one to another, let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt (Numbers 14:4), and bade stone Caleb and Joshua with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle before all the children of Israel (Numbers 14:10). The men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord (Numbers 14:37), the ten of them, while Joshua and Caleb, of the men that went to search the land, lived still (Numbers 14:38). The nation's sentence is entered separately, but it is measured from this act: after the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities (Numbers 14:34). Forty-five years later Caleb, at eighty-five, asked for the mountain the ten had feared and took it (Joshua 14:10-12), and Mattathias on his deathbed put the two together as the pattern for his sons: Caleb for bearing witness before the congregation received the heritage of the land, and Joshua for fulfilling the word was made a judge in Israel (1 Maccabees 2:55-56).

entries.commentary: The Lord told Moses to send men to search the land of Canaan, one ruler of every tribe of their fathers. Among them were Caleb the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah, and Oshea the son of Nun, whom Moses called Jehoshua, that is Joshua. Sending out spies to learn the landscape, the people, and their strength is the wisdom of war; Moses had learned such things as a leader in Egypt.

Moses sent them up to see the land, whether the people were strong or weak, few or many, the cities open or walled, the land fat or lean; and they searched it forty days. They came to the brook of Eshcol and cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes, and bare it between two upon a staff. The cluster was so great it took two men to carry it, for the earth was younger then and brought forth greater stature in its fruit and its men.

They returned and reported the land floweth with milk and honey, and showed the fruit; nevertheless the people be strong, the cities walled and very great, and the children of Anak were there. Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we; and they brought up an evil report, calling it a land that eateth up the inhabitants, where they saw the giants, the sons of Anak, and were in their own sight as grasshoppers. The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the people wept that night, and murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness. Because of the evil report, they said, Wherefore hath the LORD brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword? and they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt, forgetting there was nothing to return to, for Pharaoh and his army were destroyed and Egypt laid waste.

Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly, and Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes and exhorted the people: the land is an exceeding good land; if the Lord delight in us, He will bring us into it; only rebel not against the Lord, neither fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us, and the Lord is with us. But all the congregation bade stone them with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle. It is the same today: when the truth is brought that the Most High loves the people and has something great for them if they repent, they do not believe it and are ready to kill the messenger, hating him that rebuketh in the gate.

The Lord said, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? He would smite them with pestilence, disinherit them, and make of Moses a greater nation. Moses interceded: the Egyptians and the nations would hear that the Lord was not able to bring the people into the land and slew them in the wilderness. He pleaded, Let the power of my Lord be great, the Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity; pardon this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast forgiven them from Egypt until now. This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed.

The Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word; but as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord. The men who had seen His glory and His miracles in Egypt and in the wilderness, and had tempted Him now these ten times, would not see the land which He sware unto their fathers. But His servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, would be brought into the land, and his seed should possess it.

The Lord asked how long He should bear with this evil congregation which murmured against Him, and declared, As ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness, all that were numbered from twenty years old and upward that murmured against Him, save Caleb and Joshua. The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

When Moses told the people these sayings, they mourned greatly, then rose up early and presumed to go up to the top of the mountain, saying, We have sinned; we will go up unto the place which the Lord hath promised. Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of the LORD? it shall not prosper; go not up, for the LORD is not among you, that ye be not smitten before your enemies. But they presumed to go up, though the ark of the covenant and Moses departed not out of the camp, and the Amalekites and the Canaanites came down and smote them and discomfited them, even unto Hormah. All they had to do was follow counsel. Their refusal was written for us, that we would learn to follow the counsel of the men the Most High sets up rather than lean on our own presumption. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness: the audience of the entire book of Deuteronomy is the Israelites. Moses spake in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, according unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them.

Moses declares this law after he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites. When the Lord told Abraham his seed would serve four hundred years, he set the time of the return by the Amorites: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full. By this point their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay Sihon their king.

Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount: the Lord set the land before them, from the mount of the Amorites to Lebanon and the great river Euphrates, to go in and possess it. The land was sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their seed after them; the Most High reiterated that covenant to the fathers over and over through Genesis, reassuring them that their seed would possess the land of Canaan. Israel entered not for their own righteousness but for the sake of the promise made to the fathers; the rebellious generation was cut off, yet their children were still brought in because the Most High sware it.

I am not able to bear you myself alone: the people were multiplied as the stars of heaven, and every one of them came with cumbrance, burden, and strife. Moses refers back to what his father in law saw in Exodus 18: Moses sat judging the people alone from morning until evening, the people waiting all day in line, because they came to him to inquire of God and be shown the statutes and laws. His father in law told him the thing was not good: judging alone would wear away both Moses and the people. The counsel was to provide able men that fear God and set them in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

The people answered that the thing was good to do, and Moses took the chief of the tribes, wise men and known, and made them captains over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers among the tribes. Rank in a congregation is biblical. With schools worldwide, every issue cannot come to one man; soldiers, officers, captains, deacons, and bishop follow the same order the fathers ordained here, and the terminology of this verse is the terminology used in the body today.

The charge to the judges: hear the causes between brethren and judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and hear the small as well as the great. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment: a poor man gets no pass for being poor, and a mighty man with money and possessions is not above the laws of the Most High; no one can buy himself out of judgment. Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's: no tough face may intimidate or sway a verdict, because it is the Most High passing the judgment through the judge. The cause too hard goes up the chain to Moses, and that chain itself was instituted here.

Israel came through that great and terrible wilderness to Kadesh-barnea, to the mountain of the Amorites, and the commandment was plain: the Lord hath set the land before thee; go up and possess it; fear not, neither be discouraged. The people asked to send men first to search out the land and bring word of the way and the cities, and the saying pleased Moses; twelve men, one of a tribe, went up to the valley of Eshcol. The spies brought of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought word again: it is a good land which the Lord our God doth give us.

Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord: they acknowledged the land was good, yet all refused except Caleb and Joshua, who had faith to go take it. They murmured in their tents that the Lord hated them and brought them out of Egypt to deliver them into the hand of the Amorites to destroy them. The spies had discouraged their hearts with the report: the people greater and taller than we, cities great and walled up to heaven, and the sons of the Anakims, the giants, in the land.

Dread not, neither be afraid of them: the Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did in Egypt before your eyes. The Amorites were no mightier than Egypt, and these same Israelites witnessed how the Lord broke Egypt to bring them out; where was their faith? The principle still applies: the body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Fear of the adversary is a spirit the Most High never gave his people; whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit.

The Lord bare Israel in the wilderness as a man doth bear his son, went before them in fire by night and in a cloud by day to search out a place to pitch their tents; yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God. That is the amazing part of this history: they saw all the miracles and were carried like a son, and still believed the Lord was setting them up to be killed by giants, when a giant has nothing on the Most High. The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

The Lord heard their words and was wroth and sware: not one of the men of that evil generation would see the good land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, because he wholly followed the Lord, and Joshua the son of Nun, who would cause Israel to inherit it. Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: at the waters the people fell into the same disbelief they had shown over and over, and Moses in his anger called them rebels and smote the rock twice when the Lord had said to speak to the rock. Anger lets the commandments slip: be angry and sin not, but when anger takes hold, a man fails to apply what he knows, and Moses failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. His judgment was to be kept out of the land. Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

The little ones, the children which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, would go in and possess the land the Most High sware to the fathers. As for that generation, the command was to turn and take their journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.

Then ye answered, We have sinned: only after the judgment fell did they want to repent, girding on weapons of war and declaring themselves ready to go up. The Lord had given chance after chance to obey and not fear, and every time the same trial brought the same unbelief; do nothing without advice, and when thou hast once done, repent not. The Lord said go not up, neither fight, for I am not among you, lest ye be smitten before your enemies; and they went up presumptuously anyway, boldly doing what they were told not to do, as recorded in [Numbers 14](/bible/numbers/14). The Amorites came out against them and chased them as bees do, and destroyed them in Seir unto Hormah. They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

The countries in the land of Canaan were distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, by lot, as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half tribe; Moses had already given the two tribes and a half their inheritance on the other side Jordan. The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, therefore no part was given unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance. The Levites were living in the suburbs, which is the towns, right among the people. They did not have a land designated to themselves; they were spread throughout all the many tribes.

Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite comes to Joshua in Gilgal and reminds him of the thing the Most High said unto Moses concerning them both in Kadeshbarnea: Caleb was forty years old when Moses sent him from Kadeshbarnea to spy out the land, and he brought word again as it was in his heart. His brethren that went up with him made the heart of the people melt, but he wholly followed the Lord his God. The men that went with him brought up an evil report, made the people afraid, and made them doubt. Caleb was not playing any games; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the Most High had already promised us the land, so he had no fear. That is the spirit that says, let us go up at once and possess it. So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

The Most High has kept Caleb alive these forty and five years, and now at fourscore and five years old he is as strong this day as he was in the day Moses sent him; as his strength was then, even so is his strength now, for war, both to go out and to come in. This man is eighty-five years old and in perfect health. Moses was the same way: a hundred and twenty years old with the strength and the vision of a young man. A lot of us are not living to a hundred and twenty, but at the same time we are making it to sixty and seventy, and at fifty we are hooked up on machines. We are all going to die at some point, but that does not mean you have to be miserable, sitting there hooked up to all kind of machines while you are here. Leadership has been pushing that we all need to take care of our bodies and our health. A lot of us deal with gluttony even though it is not a topic we talk about all the time; cut down a little what you eat and eat better food. The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

Caleb asks for the very mountain the Anakims were in: now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day, for thou heardest how the Anakims were there and the cities were great and fenced; if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out. Joshua blessed him and gave Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance, and it became his inheritance unto this day, because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel. The name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba, which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war.

verses.text: And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it.
Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.
The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan.
And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.

And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature.
And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.

And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness!
And wherefore hath the Lord brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword, that our wives and our children should be a prey? were it not better for us to return into Egypt?
And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.
And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes:
And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.
If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.
Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not.
But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.
And the men, which Moses sent to search the land, who returned, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up a slander upon the land,
Even those men that did bring up the evil report upon the land, died by the plague before the Lord.
But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of the men that went to search the land, lived still.
Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord your God:
And ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because the Lord hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Whither shall we go up? our brethren have discouraged our heart, saying, The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakims there.

Then the children of Judah came unto Joshua in Gilgal: and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite said unto him, Thou knowest the thing that the Lord said unto Moses the man of God concerning me and thee in Kadesh–barnea.
Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh–barnea to espy out the land; and I brought him word again as it was in mine heart.
Nevertheless my brethren that went up with me made the heart of the people melt: but I wholly followed the Lord my God.
And Moses sware on that day, saying, Surely the land whereon thy feet have trodden shall be thine inheritance, and thy children’s for ever, because thou hast wholly followed the Lord my God.

And now, behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years, even since the Lord spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old.
As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in.

Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the Lord said.
Jesus for fulfilling the word was made a judge in Israel.
Caleb for bearing witness before the congregation received the heritage of the land.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
When faced with the alternative of battle we are not to be afraid of strong enemies.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.
